content.comment_body: [product_name] [version_no] without display. I’m confused by the system behavior. During the online test, everything looks correct, but in practice it’s different. Outputs Q1 to Q6 provide a visual overview of the solar panel power. Manual boiler startup is signaled by Q11 when the thermostat demands heat, regardless of PV production. In the online test, I1 is always active, unlike the mechanical setup. Q3 remains constantly lit. When I activate I8, Q3 turns off and Q4 comes on—even though I8 isn’t actually used in the program. Could this [product_name] be malfunctioning and operating unpredictably? I’m unsure how to upload a rar file now.
The file extension ".rar" isn’t accepted. You could upload your project as a zip file instead.

From a programming perspective, Q3 shouldn’t be on unless Q1 and Q2 are also on. Hardware fault in the main module is unlikely. I8 is not programmed to affect Q3. Judging from your detailed description, a wiring mistake seems the most probable cause.

Thanks a lot for your reply. Wiring hasn’t changed. Issues started only after I modified the IP address of the [product_name] control unit. Afterward, I reloaded each [product_name]. Interestingly, in the online test, I1 is off, but nothing physical happens. I8 on the control board no longer affects Q4. I’ll wait for sunlight to further troubleshoot.

Update: I created a simple program—with just inputs and outputs—to test. No results: [product_name] doesn’t respond. When running an online test from my PC, I get this message: Online test failed. The hardware type of [product_name] in [product_name]Soft Comfort does not match the physical [product_name] device.
This means the selected hardware in your [product_name] configuration is not compatible with your actual [product_name] device.

In my browser, I see: System Control Device Series [product_name] [article_no] Device Type 230RCEo FW [version_no] IP 192.168.0.60 Status: Running System Meter box Device Series [product_name] [article_no] Device Type 12/24RCEo FW [version_no] IP 192.168.0.61 Status: Running System Attic Device Series [product_name] [article_no] Device Type 12/24RCEo FW [version_no] IP 192.168.0.62 Status: Running System Boiler Device Series [product_name] [article_no] Device Type 12/24RCEo FW [version_no] IP 192.168.0.63 Status: Running System Shutters (only one with display) Device Series [product_name] [article_no] Device Type 12/24RCE FW [version_no] IP 192.168.0.64 Status: Running I recently changed the IPs of Boiler and Control. The Boiler [product_name] is the 230V version. Is that the problem? Or is the Control [product_name] still malfunctioning?
Which type is the Boiler [product_name] now: 12/24 RCEo or 230 RCEo?
Boiler [product_name] is a 230RCEo—it’s always been that version.

I’m worried I may have jeopardized my whole setup. Turns out the wiring was incorrect before; now it’s fixed. I also managed to set the fixed IP addresses. To play it safe, I bought a new [product_name] for control (version [version_no] now). It functions, but new issues have appeared: I can’t connect the meter box and control units. There’s always a blocked symbol when trying, even for the boiler connection (no access to B014). It all used to work fine. The power grid (Grid PWR) setup seems okay—it eventually started working. Meterkast (meter box) control B006 -> B006 B005 -> B007 B004 -> B008 Any ideas? Also, what’s the difference between mnp and snp?
With [product_name] [version_no]: You need to enable S7 access in the file properties. Without this, [product_name] [version_no] can’t communicate with other [product_name] units via S7.

I’m not sure what you’re attempting. You’re mixing two methods for creating connections: a) Drag-and-drop between files. b) Manual setup via VM, but no connection created between [product_name] units, so there’s no connection data. Plus, you use the same word in the VM area (VW0) for three different values—a source of problems.
That’s what’s strange—drag and drop isn’t working, always gives the blocked circle. Therefore, I manually created analog network blocks in the diagram to clarify the connections I want to make.
I don’t know exactly what steps you took but it’s working now. I should now be able to send "Solar PWR" data to the "boiler" myself. Many thanks!
I deleted the NAIs and NAQs and rewired using drag and drop without problems.

Not sure what happened before. Now, I was able to establish a drag-and-drop connection between Solar PWR and B014 from Boiler without any issue. Sometimes these setups take some trial and error to understand.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced discrepancies between the online test results and the actual system performance after updating IP addresses and reloading configurations across multiple [product_name] controllers operating solar panels and a boiler. The test simulations did not match physical behavior, causing outputs and inputs to respond unexpectedly. Troubleshooting identified a hardware configuration mismatch between [product_name]Soft Comfort and the real device, leading to further connection failures and system errors.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects reliable and consistent correspondence between simulation results and hardware responses, straightforward configuration management, and clear diagnostic feedback when encountering any issues.
